  Inspection History

Please Note:  Deficiencies on an inspection that are deemed “non-critical” by the Public Health Officer are required to be remedied by the next scheduled inspection and may remain displayed until that time. A “non-critical” deficiency is a violation of the Legislation that presents a minimal health risk. Examples are: Walls, floors or other non-food contact surfaces or equipment need cleaning or repair.

Date Inspected: 24 Sep, 2026
This establishment was inspected by the Nova Scotia Environment Inspection, Compliance and Enforcement Division, and the following deficiencies and/or Warning Reports were issued at the time of the inspection:
DeficiencyStatus
19(2)(a) - FAILING TO PROVIDE POTABLE HOT & COLD WATER AT ADEQUATE PRESSURE AND VOLUME WITH APPROPRIATE FACILITIES TO STORE AND DISTRIBUTE WATER AND CONTROL TEMPERATURE.DEFICIENT
Remedy
Post Boil Water Advisory sign at handwash sink to advise users. Education given on proper manual equipment sanitizing step. Operator to ensure proper wash, rinse, sanitize, & air dry steps are followed. Do not use water in ice or beverages unless boiled then cooled or commercially bottled water used. Follow all Water Use During a Boil Advisory precautions. See NSE Water Lead Inspector for corrections required (including new well cap that is verminproof). Have Water Lead Inspector remove Boil Water Advisory within 3 weeks of original advisory. Perform any resampling required.
 
DeficiencyStatus
29(2)(a) - INADEQUATE MAINTENANCE, CLEANING, & SANITATION PROGRAM. DEFICIENT
Remedy
Provide waste bin / shed that is verminproof to store all wastes and recycling. Provide additional storage shelving / platforms so all food and packaging is stored properly and >= 6in. / 15 cm. off of the floor. Make skirting on building verminproof.
Date Inspected: 18 Dec, 2025
This establishment was inspected by the Nova Scotia Environment Inspection, Compliance and Enforcement Division, and the following deficiencies and/or Warning Reports were issued at the time of the inspection:
DeficiencyStatus
29(2)(a) - INADEQUATE MAINTENANCE, CLEANING, & SANITATION PROGRAM.NON CRITICAL
Remedy
Acquire acceptable sanitizer product and use as per. manufacturer's instruction. Pre-clean surfaces and then use sanitizer on a regular frequency, with change of use of area, and when needed, for all food contact and hand contact surfaces.
